title: Puerto Rico Medicaid Task Force Report 2027: Making the Case for the Obvious. Another Report, the Same Emergency.
description: Roughly 40% of Puerto Rico relies on Medicaid, almost double the 21% average in the states, and the program runs on a capped Section 1108 allotment instead of the open-ended federal match every state gets. The temporary 2023 fix lifted the island's match from 55% to 76% and raised the ceiling to $3.825 billion; when it expires, the match falls back to 55% and about $3.36 billion a year leaves the system, putting 860,000 to 1 million people at risk of losing coverage and pushing the uninsured rate from 5.7% to roughly 30%. The October 2026 task force report lays out the rest: an aging, poorer and sicker population, a $74-a-month disability benefit where SSI would pay up to $994, no home- and community-based long-term care, and a trauma hospital running at a -3.7% margin. Underfunding already costs more: Medicaid spends $3,293 per enrollee in Puerto Rico against $10,377 in the median state, so the 15,303 eligible people who moved to the mainland in 2024 cost the federal government $96.8 million instead of $41.8 million. Puerto Rico has met every CMS integrity requirement and earns an extra $375 million a year for compliance. The closing question: is the cap saving money, or just moving the bill to someone else's balance sheet?
short_title: Puerto Rico Medicaid Task Force Report 2027: Making the Case for the Obvious
